page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-8GB is a virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor. The configuration features 4 vCPUs with shared CPU allocation, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 40 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also achieve top-tier results. However, multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores, fall into the average category. Memory performance is a notable tradeoff, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the bottom 25%, though cached memory read bandwidth reaches 850.79 GB/sec.

This server type represents a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring strong single-threaded performance but moderate memory capacity. The shared CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio make it suitable for lightweight web serving, software compilation, text processing, and small-scale LLM text generation. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases or large-scale multi-threaded applications due to its shared resource model and lower memory tier.
